questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

Education, no doubt, _______ bring about the all-round development of a child.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"aims to". **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Here's the explanation for each option:**

 
 
• **"Aims for" - **This phrase is used when there is a particular goal or target that one wants to achieve.

 
 
• However, considering that the sentence is about the purpose (not the goal) of education, this option isn't the most suitable.
 
 
 
• **"Aim at" - **This phrase is used to mean targeting in a physical sense, or directing effort or a criticism towards a literal or metaphorical target.
 
 
• It's not the best fit for the sentence because education isn't 'aiming at' something, it's carrying out a purpose.
 
 
 
• **"Get rid at" **- This phrase is grammatically incorrect.
 
 
• If we're discussing eliminating something, the correct term would be **"get rid of", **not **"get rid at". **
 
• However, this isn't suitable here because the sentence isn't about getting rid of something.
 
 
 
• **"Aims to" **- This phrase is used to express an objective or purpose that someone or something intends to achieve.
 
 
• This perfectly fits the context, showing the purpose of education.
 
 
 
 
 
• Therefore, the complete sentence reads: **"Education, no doubt, aims to bring about the all-round development of a child." **
 
• It explains that one of the main purposes of education is to foster holistic development in a child.
 
• So, **"aims to" **is the most appropriate option to fill the blank.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 4".**

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Machines can only __accomplish a maximum set of tasks__, as machines do not hold any thought process of their own.

options.text: accomplish a valued set of tasks
accomplish a gist set of tasks
accomplish a restricted set of tasks
accomplish a difficult set of tasks

questions.solution:
The correct answer is "accomplish a restricted set of tasks". 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the sentence, **"Machines can only accomplish a maximum set of tasks, as machines do not hold any thought process of their own," **the underlined segment is **"accomplish a maximum set of tasks". **

 
 
• **​**It indicates the scope or extent of tasks that machinery is able to perform with its inherent limitations, since machines lack independent thinking abilities.
 
 
 
• **Looking at the options provided:**
 
 
• **"accomplish a valued set of tasks" **- this phrase implies that the tasks have some inherent value, but it does not indicate that there's an upper limit to what machines can do, which is a key point in the original sentence.
 
• **"accomplish a gist set of tasks" - **the term **"gist" **means the essence or the main point of something. Here, it would not make sense as machines perform specific tasks rather than the **"gist" **of tasks.
 
• **"accomplish a restricted set of tasks" - **this phrase correctly conveys the idea that there is a certain limit to the tasks that machinery can complete due to their lack of own thought processes, making this option a fitting substitute for the original segment.
 
• **"accomplish a difficult set of tasks" - **this signifies the level of complexity in tasks, not the limit that machines have in their capabilities.
 
 
 
• Therefore, the best option that substitutes the underlined segment in the given sentence is: **"accomplish a restricted set of tasks"**
 
• Thus, the revised sentence reads: **"Machines can only *accomplish a restricted set of tasks, __*as machines do not hold any thought process of their own."**

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 3".**

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

He said that / he had want / to read a / novel by Enid Blyton.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: "**he had want**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The segment that contains a **grammatical error** is: "**he had want**"
 
• The **correct version** should be: "**he had wanted**"
 
• In the sentence, the verb "**had**" is used as an **auxiliary verb** indicating past perfect tense, and it is followed by the base form of the verb "**want**."
 
• However, in English, when using the **past perfect tense**, the **past participle** form of the verb is required after the auxiliary verb "**had**."
 
• The past participle of "**want**" is "**wanted**," so the correct construction in the past perfect tense is "**he had wanted**."
 
• The **past perfect tense** is** formed by** combining **the past tense of the auxiliary verb "have" (had) with the past participle of the main verb ("wanted")**.
 
• This tense is used to indicate an action that was completed before another past action.
 
• Therefore, the **corrected sentence** is: *He said that he had wanted to read a novel by Enid Blyton.*

Thus, **option 1** is the correct answer.
